searchText: how many users can Ethereum safely support on rollups? Im thinking if a rollup ended up with 200,000 users. Or more. But then it went offline and everyone had to do the escape hatch thing. Would it even be possible? i guess it can support millions of people but it would still be a bidding war to get ur funds out This was one of the problems with Plasma. You had to exit within a finite period of time and it is possible that a rush of exits could clog the network so not everyone could exit if that time was too short. ZK Rollups are ideal on this front because there is no time limit on exiting or paying attention. You can show up years later and still exit, even if the entire system went offline. (assuming you have access to the necessary tooling and data) im assuming this tooling and data would not be easy to come by for the average user but there could just be restoration services then. i mean the person who did go out of his way to secure this tooling and data could help others. for a fee perhaps or something Yep. They charge fee for every NFT trade, that's their fee. IDK if they charge fee for NFT mint too. They claim that in the future they're gonna support transfering NFT to L1, but have no ETA for that. So, until that changes, any NFT u have on IMX is locked there. so what im getting at is that zkrollups seems too good to be true. basically your deposit will always be insured against failure on the service in questions part. and this insurance is supposedly free. Something does not add up The downside to zkRollups is the insanely complicated math, almost no tooling (though this is getting better), and the high cost of proof generation. The math/tooling will eventually be abstracted/solved, but the high proof generation costs may end up being a limiter at some point. i am presuming it will be a limitor in the way that the service in question would have higher computation costs and therefore higher prices. for example DyDx would not be able to have as low fees as coinbase since its computation costs will be higher due to using zkRollup tech. But on the other hand users deposits will have probably the best insurance you can have (the escape hatch thing.) + no kyc and so on. and it probably will win depending on how much it costs to run a service on/with zkrollup tech with lots of users. interesting With a rollup, only one person needs to generate the proof. That person can use a super-computer to do so, and we don't need to trust that person to be honest. This is the saving grace behind the high proof generation costs. i dont think its gonna be able to compete with CEX tbh. DyDx that is It is possible (maybe even likely) that the cost of running the proof generator is insignificant compared to all of the other costs. Similar to how the cost of running Coinbase servers is likely insignificant compared to their other operational costs. The L1 data availability stuff will still have non-zero costs, unlike internal Coinbase transfers. yes thats it. i think. when you made a trade on DyDx they have to update your balance. and imagine thousands of users doing trades and these balances have to be updated in realtime? if they dont then the point kinda is lost those updates will not be cheap computational wise if its zkrollup. where as coinbase will be able to it much cheaper becaues they dont do zkrollup. but i could be wrong. The cost of the proof generation likely will be insignificant compared to the L1 gas costs of data availability for the rollup. Optimism's idea is to just reuse geth sync if we are completely honest rollups are not really scaling solutions they are more like dapps but i could be wrong yeah you're pretty wrong right now the tooling kinda sucks but that's just because they're immature rollups intended for *trading* yeah I agree but general purpose ones like zksync are really intended to be general purpose payments platforms right so all rollups are dapps but not all rollup dapps are focused on payments I would phrase it as: "rollups are scaling solutions (that you can interact with via native dapps or other more general tools)" i wonder if the layer2 rhetoric will be deprecated like "ETH 2.0" was 🙂 who knows like I expect that wallets in 5 years to transparently move funds around between rollups automatically as needed and users won't need to know anything about what's going on under the hood unless they want to Current solutions are proprietary and only their owners run instances. They are better than centralized exchanges because they are permissionless to withdraw funds, but they have higher computational costs. I wouldn't say they're "proprietary" they're just not cross-compatible I dont think dydx can remain permissionless tho. how come they are able to have US customers? Their instance is not decentralized im pretty sure it will just take an email from the SEC or whatever to the DyDx team and they will begin requiring KYC but i could be wrong proprietary as opposed to open source The advantage of centralized exchanges is that they keep higher popularity as long as ppl need to use them to transfer fiat, so there will always be ppl willing to remain on them anyway. They're also cross-network. And ppl that like to have somebody fixing their mistakes can also ask help to cex support. I see L2 as they are now as centalized server/instance where dApps are deployed and run. They have higher computational cost than RDBMS, but they are permissionless on the L1. On a off-chain service, assets are owned by the service's sc. On L2, assets are owned by us. As long as L2 instances are centralized, their owners and dApps deployed on them are subject to legislation. Financial authority may require them to do KYC. I think we should stop calling rollups L2 and just call them rollups but that doesent even seem accurate they are just dapps lol sry I don't see rollups are dApps, I see them as instances that run dApps I understand L1 as the native blockchain(s) and L2 as any off-chain instance that commits to L1 some sort of data to assure security. i wonder if coinbase fits that definition it does not isn't it a cex? coinbase derives trust from outside L2s derive trust from the ledger they are based upon well coinbase is off-chain and it commits data to L1 every now and then when user requests withdrawal I hope eventually somebody will develop FOSS rollups but when assets are on them, blockchain see these assets as owned by them, not by their customers customers need their permission to withdraw, they're able to deny it but the trust isn't derived from the chain it's through the legal framework you enter when you use coinbase I don't see L2 ending with ETH shards. I haven't seen any1 say ETH gas price will drop or tps will scale higher than the number of shards. I think they're gonna remain and will eventually run most complex dApps. L2 for simple FTs like Synthetix use case may not be needed, but for NFT games they will remain. shards aren't L2 yep oh I misinterpreted what you were saying I wonder if ETH shards will be able to do atomic swaps or if we'll need to transfer tokens among shards so we can make trades. my belief is that the entire ERC20 spec needs to be thrown out to better support multiple coordinated token contracts servicing one asset across all shards yep, but they wanna keep retrocompatibility and then someone can have a shim to wrap that spec in a shard-local ERC20 asset if they want We may have a new multi-shard-friendly standard for new stuff, but they want PoW sc to keep working on the PoS. I also think it's a bad idea to have Beacon chain inheriting PoW blockchain. I think Beacon chain should be lean and only coordinate shards, and The Merge should create a shard that inherits PoW chain. Then we could develop a new standard to make atomic swaps easier/possible. This would make L2 less needed. it's waaay too late to argue in favor of that yep I know
